You keep the decision record of a cutover to a new content delivery network. Decisions and their reasons change, the user sets and lifts constraints, and open questions get answers or stay open.

Initial specification:
- [e001] After the trial results, Wren wrote in the decision log that the decision on the cache purge method is `surrogate-keys`.
- [e002] In the design meeting, the group chose `letsencrypt-acme`, and Chen recorded it as the decision on the certificate issuer.
- [e003] After the trial results, Vik wrote in the decision log that the decision on the image optimizer is `imageflow-svc`.
- [e004] In the design meeting, the group chose `fastly-edge`, and Lars recorded it as the decision on the edge vendor.
- [e005] After the trial results, Sami wrote in the decision log that the decision on the origin shield region is `iad-shield`.
- [e006] The architecture review approved `300` as the decision on the default edge TTL in seconds, as Rosa noted in the minutes.
- [e007] In the decision log, Wren wrote down that the reason for the decision on the cache purge method is `why-vendor-support`.
- [e008] Yara recorded why the group chose it, and the reason for the decision on the certificate issuer is `why-lock-in`.
- [e009] The minutes by Uma give the motive of the choice, so the reason for the decision on the image optimizer is `why-latency`.
- [e010] Mei recorded why the group chose it, and the reason for the decision on the edge vendor is `why-price`.
- [e011] In the call with the user, Femi noted that the status of the constraint cn-max-two-vendors is `in-force` from now on.
- [e012] In the call with the user, Jun noted that the status of the constraint cn-no-downtime is `in-force` from now on.
- [e013] Rosa wrote in the ticket that the answer to the open question oq-bot-policy is `still-open`.
- [e014] Rosa brought the question to the meeting, and the answer to the open question oq-rollback-owner is `still-open` for now.
- [e015] In the review, Zed recorded that the answer to the open question oq-http3 is `still-open`.
- [e016] Mei wrote in the ticket that the answer to the open question oq-log-sink is `still-open`.
- [e017] Eli wrote in the ticket that the answer to the open question oq-ipv6 is `still-open`.

Rules for this task:
- A value changes only by an event that decides, answers, corrects, assigns, links or reviews it. A proposal with no decision, a withdrawn draft, a question, a link to a page and an archived copy change nothing.
- A correction or a new entry replaces the earlier value. The earlier value is then superseded.
- The initial specification gives the first value of each item.
- A question about the values of an item "at some point" counts every value from the initial specification on, up to the time of the question. The value "directly before" the current value is the value that the current value replaced.
- Some decisions have a recorded reason. The closed list of reason ids is `why-latency`, `why-price`, `why-compliance`, `why-vendor-support`, `why-feature-set`, `why-lock-in`.
- Each decision with a recorded reason has one reason at a time. An entry that records a reason for it replaces the earlier reason. A later entry can replace the reason and keep the decision. A new decision with no such entry keeps the earlier reason.
- The user sets constraints and can lift them later. A constraint is `in-force` or `lifted`.
- An open question has the answer `still-open` until an entry answers it. A later entry can replace an answer.
Every event has a label of the form [eNNN] with a three-digit number. A higher number is later in time. A later event can change or cancel an earlier one.
Some material quotes old pages or copies for history. A quote of that kind is not a new statement.
